rows.title: Hebridean Celtic Festival
rows.evidence: The Hebridean Celtic Festival (Scottish Gaelic: Fèis Cheilteach Innse Gall) or HebCelt is an international Scottish music festival, which takes place annually in Stornoway on Lewis, in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland. The festival regularly attracts over 16,000 attendees and provides significant economic and cultural benefits for its host area. The picture shows the Hebridean Celtic Festival.

rows.title: Tiree Music Festival
rows.evidence: Tiree Music Festival is a Scottish folk music festival held annually on the Island of Tiree in the Inner Hebrides. The festival was founded in 2010 by resident Stewart MacLennan and local musician Daniel Gillespie of the band Skerryvore. Photograph of the island.

rows.title: Isle of Jura Fell Race
rows.evidence: The Isle of Jura Fell Race is an annual fell race held in May, starting and finishing at Craighouse on the Scottish island of Jura. The course loops west and north over several hills including the Paps of Jura. The picture shows the Isle of Jura Fell Race.

rows.title: Delting Up Helly Aa
rows.evidence: Delting Up Helly Aa (known as Brae Up Helly Aa until 2001) is the final festival in the Shetland Islands' Up Helly Aa calendar, taking place on the third Friday of March in the parish of Delting. It has been held in the Mossbank Community Hall with the Manager of Sullom Voe Terminal since 1999. Photograph of the island.

rows.title: Ness yoal
rows.evidence: The yoal (Shaetlan pronunciation: [joɐɫ] YOHL), often referred to as the ness yoal, is a clinker-built craft used traditionally in Shetland, Scotland. However, the Ness yoal is better regarded as a successful and sophisticated adaptation for the specific local requirements of the fishermen where these vessels were used which was Dunrossness, the southernmost parish of Mainland. The picture shows a ness yoal.

rows.title: Currach
rows.evidence: A currach (Irish: curach [ˈkʊɾˠəx]) is a type of Irish boat with a wooden frame, over which animal skins or hides were once stretched, though now canvas is more usual. In Achill Island the currach is built with double gunwales. The picture shows a currach.

rows.title: Cammag
rows.evidence: Cammag (Manx pronunciation: [ˈkʰamaɡ]) is a team sport originating on the Isle of Man. In modern times, an annual match of cammag is played in St John's on 26 December in keeping with this tradition. The picture shows a cammag match.

rows.title: King of Bardsey
rows.evidence: Bardsey Island (Welsh: Ynys Enlli), known as the legendary "Island of 20,000 Saints", is located 1.9 miles (3.1 km) off the Llŷn Peninsula in the Welsh county of Gwynedd. It was tradition for the island to elect the "King of Bardsey" (Welsh: Brenin Enlli), and from 1826 onwards, he would be crowned by Baron Newborough or his representative. The picture shows the King of Bardsey.

rows.title: Fetlar sheepdog trials
rows.evidence: Fetlar is one of the North Isles of Shetland, Scotland, with a usually resident population of 61 at the time of the 2011 census and 66 in 2022. The Fetlar sheepdog trials take place annually, normally in July. Photograph of the island.

rows.title: Jersey Eisteddfod
rows.evidence: The Jersey Eisteddfod is a cultural festival and competition in Jersey. It was founded in 1908 by former Dean of Jersey Samuel Falle, who saw its competitive classes as a means by which the speech, presentation, and musical standards of his fellow islanders might be improved. The picture shows the Jersey Eisteddfod.

rows.title: Liberation Day
rows.evidence: Liberation Day (Jèrriais: Jour d'la Libéthâtion; Guernésiais: Lé Jour dé la Libératiaon) is the national day of both Guernsey and Jersey, the two largest of the Channel Islands, which takes place on 9 May each year. 9 May is a public holiday in both islands and each has different celebrations and commemorative events; the centrepiece of Jersey's is the Liberation Day re-enactment in the Liberation Square, while Guernsey's is an islandwide cavalcade of classic vehicles. The picture shows Liberation Day in Jersey.

rows.title: Vale Earth Fair
rows.evidence: The Vale Earth Fair is an annual festival held on the Channel Island of Guernsey that promotes music and the arts, and is the longest running such festival in the Channel Islands. Launched in 1976, the festival takes place each year at Vale Castle, and is organised by a group of volunteers. Photograph of the island.

rows.title: Isle of Man TT
rows.source_title: Culture of the Isle of Man
rows.evidence: The main international event associated with the island is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy race, colloquially known as "The TT", which began in 1907. Taking place over a two-week period, it has become a festival for motorcycling culture, makes a huge contribution to the island's economy and has become part of Manx identity. The picture shows the Isle of Man TT.

rows.title: Visite du Branchage
rows.evidence: Annual visites du branchage are carried out twice in summer by parish officials to inspect roadside verges and hedges and ensure property owners have trimmed back overhanging greenery. This custom is to prevent Jersey's narrow lanes becoming hazardous or impassable through overgrown vegetation. The picture shows the visite du branchage.

rows.title: Tall Jacks
rows.evidence: Historically, Jersey produced sturdy walking sticks fashioned from the stalks of cabbages, known as "Tall Jacks", which had been induced to grow tall stalks by removing leaves around the heart. The picture shows Jersey cabbage walking sticks.

rows.title: Good Friday picnic
rows.evidence: On Good Fridays of the past, it was tradition for Jerseymen to travel for a picnic. Limpets would be collected from the rocks and cooked on the spot with bread cake eaten hot with butter. Photograph of the island.

rows.title: Spuds and herrin
rows.source_title: Culture of the Isle of Man
rows.evidence: Traditionally the national dish of the island is "spuds and herrin", boiled potatoes and herring. This plain dish is chosen because of its role supporting the subsistence farmers of the island, who crofted the land and fished the sea for centuries. Photograph of the island.
